title: Q-ASHBY-habituation: recognise a detector that keeps firing with no change of state
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe habituation
**Status:** closed

Problem: A failure-mode probe that goes red, is reopened and goes red again with the same outcome produces the same item each time. Ashby's journal (index: Habituation, J.4524 to J.4535, fundamental theorems J.5512 and J.5674; the operator matters, not the machine, J.5702) shows that a repeated disturbance that changes nothing comes to produce less response, and that this depends on the operator repeated.

Build: Add `export function habituation(firings)` to `seed/worker/src/ashby.js` (firings: the times a detector fired and whether state changed between them; returns the run of identical firings and whether the response has decayed). In `seed/worker/src/selfaudit.js`, a mode that has fired 5 times in 14 days with no kept change between firings files one `HABITUATED-<mode>` item for the portfolio manager (change the detector or the remedy) and stops refiling the same fix. Tests in `seed/worker/test/ashby.test.js` and `seed/worker/test/selfaudit.test.js`. Bind the concept `habituation` in `doctrine/ashby-concepts.json`.

**Prediction:** ashby_gaps <= 3 within 720 h

**Out of scope:** silencing a detector; changing any probe's SQL; modes that changed state between firings.

size: M

**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe habituation` passes when the concept is implemented and every mechanism it names exists (ASHBY-KERNEL-1).

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-27T10:02:06Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.1 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
